The goal is to minimize the total transportation cost while ensuring that all cities receive the resources they need, without exceeding the capacity of the transportation links or the storage capacity of the cities.

City 0 has a net demand of 2 units, City 1 has a balanced supply and demand, City 2 has a net supply of 1 unit, City 3 has a net demand of 2 units, City 4 has a net supply of 2 units, City 5 has a balanced supply and demand, City 6 has a net demand of 1 unit, and City 7 has a net supply of 2 units.

The cost of transporting resources from City 0 to City 1 is 1 unit, to City 2 is 1 unit, to City 3 is 1 unit, to City 4 is 1 unit, to City 5 is 3 units, to City 6 is 3 units, and to City 7 is 3 units. From City 1 to City 0 is 1 unit, to City 2 is 2 units, to City 3 is 2 units, to City 4 is 2 units, to City 5 is 3 units, to City 6 is 2 units, and to City 7 is 1 unit. From City 2 to City 0 is 2 units, to City 1 is 3 units, to City 3 is 3 units, to City 4 is 2 units, to City 5 is 2 units, to City 6 is 3 units, and to City 7 is 3 units. The maximum capacity for transporting resources from City 0 to City 1 is 7 units, to City 2 is 9 units, to City 3 is 7 units, to City 4 is 8 units, to City 5 is 9 units, to City 6 is 7 units, and to City 7 is 7 units. From City 1 to City 0 is 8 units, to City 2 is 8 units, to City 3 is 8 units, to City 4 is 7 units, to City 5 is 9 units, to City 6 is 8 units, and to City 7 is 9 units. The maximum storage capacity for City 0 is 16 units, City 1 is 16 units, City 2 is 18 units, City 3 is 12 units, City 4 is 14 units, City 5 is 16 units, City 6 is 12 units, and City 7 is 14 units.

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    cities = d["cities"]
    arcs = list(d["cost"].keys())

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.I = pyo.Set(initialize=cities)
    model.A = pyo.Set(initialize=arcs, dimen=2)

    # assumption: variable_domain NonNegativeReals; "determine the optimal amount of resources to transport between cities"
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.A, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # "minimize the total transportation cost"
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["cost"][(i, j)] * m.x[i, j] for (i, j) in arcs)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # "each city's net demand or supply is satisfied": outbound - inbound == net_demand
    def balance_rule(m, i):
        outbound = sum(m.x[i, j] for (a, j) in arcs if a == i)
        inbound = sum(m.x[j, i] for (j, a) in arcs if a == i)
        return outbound - inbound == d["net_demand"][i]

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=balance_rule)

    # "without exceeding the capacity of the transportation links": x[i,j] <= link_capacity[i,j]
    def link_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.x[i, j] <= d["link_capacity"][(i, j)]

    model.link_cap = pyo.Constraint(model.A, rule=link_rule)

    # "the storage capacities of the cities are not exceeded": inbound + outbound <= storage_capacity
    def storage_rule(m, i):
        outbound = sum(m.x[i, j] for (a, j) in arcs if a == i)
        inbound = sum(m.x[j, i] for (j, a) in arcs if a == i)
        return inbound + outbound <= d["storage_capacity"][i]

    model.storage = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=storage_rule)

    return model

        0: 16, 1: 16, 2: 18, 3: 12, 4: 14, 5: 16, 6: 12, 7: 14,
    },
}

GOLD_ANSWER = None


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.I = pyo.Set(initialize=d["cities"])          # cities
    model.A = pyo.Set(initialize=d["arcs"], dimen=2)   # directed transportation arcs

    # "determine the optimal amount of resources to transport between cities"
    # assumption: variable_domain NonNegativeReals
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.A, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # "minimize the total transportation cost"
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["cost"][(i, j)] * m.x[i, j] for (i, j) in d["arcs"])

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # "each city's net demand or supply is satisfied"
    # outbound - inbound == net_demand
    def balance_rule(m, i):
        outbound = sum(m.x[i, j] for j in d["cities"] if (i, j) in d["cost"])
        inbound = sum(m.x[j, i] for j in d["cities"] if (j, i) in d["cost"])
        return outbound - inbound == d["net_demand"][i]

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=balance_rule)

    # "without exceeding the capacity of the transportation links"
    # x[i,j] <= link_capacity[i,j]
    def link_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.x[i, j] <= d["link_capacity"][(i, j)]

    model.link_cap = pyo.Constraint(model.A, rule=link_rule)

    # "the storage capacities of the cities are not exceeded"
    # assumption: storage_capacity_interpretation inbound - outbound + net_demand <= storage_capacity
    def storage_rule(m, i):
        outbound = sum(m.x[i, j] for j in d["cities"] if (i, j) in d["cost"])
        inbound = sum(m.x[j, i] for j in d["cities"] if (j, i) in d["cost"])
        return inbound - outbound + d["net_demand"][i] <= d["storage_capacity"][i]

    model.storage = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=storage_rule)

    return model
